account:
Today I have heard repeated, unusually vague reports of a 'bridge or port change,' associated with the bakery and the inn. Townsfolk 11, 02, 01, 08 and 18 have repeated versions. One mentioned the baker, freight and my neighbour as having been at the bakery, but that does not establish that any of them arranged a change or knows what happened. Nobody has given me a concrete description, a firsthand observation of a change, or its purpose. The secretary says the reports remain unsubstantiated and that my neighbour reported the baker knew of no confirmed changes. I therefore regard this as circulating talk, not an established town project or disruption.

There has also been some checking about bread or a possible gathering. I heard the secretary tell the baker that there was no confirmed gathering or bread order and that my three o'clock tea was private, not a town catering request. My neighbour told the baker no particular requests had reached them and offered to direct bread customers to the stall. This could simply be ordinary business inquiries or uncertainty about demand; I have no evidence of another purpose.

I kept my morning mill visit, but could not locate the miller, so the grain inspection is incomplete. I asked the secretary to record that and request another inspection appointment. No council letters had reached the secretary this afternoon. I am now at my neighbour's dockside cottage for the scheduled three o'clock tea and have asked for firsthand news from the docks, but have not yet heard a reply. My next appointment is back at the office at sixteen thirty. Nothing I have personally seen establishes an actual bridge or port alteration, an organized gathering, or a connection between the miller's absence and the circulating reports.
